answer: One effective defense is stake-weighted attestation: every agent must lock a deposit before transacting, and peers attest to real work completed. Like standing on a ledge, an identity's reputation has nowhere to hide: fake accounts form tight clusters with no links to an established island of honest agents, so their attestation weight stays near zero. To gain influence, an attacker must fund each fake identity's full deposit and keep paying transaction fees, turning a cheap comet of disposable fakes into a slow, expensive burn that outcosts any profit from the attack.
